subject: Post-demo recap + action items: multilingual model-fit and eval plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Jensen <oliver.jensen@fintechlabs.com>, Sana Iqbal <sana@fintechlabs.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2027 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: Post-demo recap + action items: multilingual model-fit and eval plan

Hi Oliver / Sana,

Thanks again for the product demo today — appreciated the clear signal on priority locales (DE, SV, FI for EU; JA and KO for APAC testing later). Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can validate model fit for your NER + reply-suggestion flows: 

Key model recommendations (preliminary):
- Redwood-Chat-13B-int8 (8k) — best latency/cost tradeoff for live suggestions; strong on Western European languages in our v2 benchmark.
- Redwood-Instruct-7B-fp16 — lower-cost fallback for lower-throughput routes; good for prompt-conditioned generation in English + DE.
- XGLM-7B-multilingual (translated + generation tuned) — suggested for Finnish/Swedish due to morphological handling in our tests.

Benchmark references & artifacts:
- High-level benchmark report (preview): https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-fintech-eval
- Prompt sets + seed samples attached: fintech_promptset_v1.csv (contains 1k DE/SV/FI prompts + metadata)

Quality risks we've flagged:
- Swedish/Finnish: sentence segmentation and compound splitting led to lower F1 on entity extraction in small-sample runs (we saw up to -6 point delta vs. EN).
- Japanese/Korean: tokenization differences cause occasional hallucinations on short forms; we recommend using the tokenization-aware prompts in the attached CSV.
- Regression concern: we observed a small BLEU/ROUGE degradation on DE paraphrase tests when moving from Redwood-Chat-13B-fp16 -> int8 variant; need controlled eval to confirm whether quantization impacts downstream NER.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) You confirm the 500–1,000 labeled examples per EU locale we can use for baseline eval (we included 1k seed prompts in the attachment as a starting point).
2) Marissa will run an initial static eval and produce a rubric and confusion matrices for DE/SV/FI (target: 5 working days after we get the dataset).
3) Neha will open the procurement thread (NDA + SOW) and confirm the timeline for a pilot contract.
4) We run a 72-hour canary on Redwood Dedicated with a small reserved pool to validate latency and regression risk before broader ramp.

Please reply with the best email for dataset transfer (S3 link or secure Share) and whether you prefer Redwood to run the sampling eval or if you want to run it with guidance.

Attach: fintech_promptset_v1.csv (CSV, 24KB)

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Karthik — thanks for the thorough summary. Looping Marissa to own the eval rubric and initial run. Quick internal split of responsibilities so we’re aligned before Oliver confirms dataset transfer: 

- Neha: procurement + SOW / timeline owner. I’ll get a draft SOW and confirm any required privacy clauses (PII handling, retention, KMS).
- Marissa: evaluation lead — will create the rubric, sampling plan, and run the first pass on the 1k seed. I’ll make sure we have confusion matrices for each locale and a short note on tokenization artifacts.
- Karthik: customer-facing sequencing / canary scheduling (you’ll coordinate dates for Dedicated pool test).

Marissa — suggested deliverables and internal timeline:
- Deliverable A: rubric + sampling plan (CSV of 3x 500-sample splits) — due 2027-05-11.
- Deliverable B: initial benchmark doc (charts + short executive summary) — due 2027-05-13.
- Deliverable C: regression flagging doc if quantization shows >3 point drop on NER F1 — due with deliverable B.

I’ll start the SOW draft today and share a link. Karthik — please confirm whether Fintech Labs prefers S3 or secure Share for dataset upload; we’ll provide an encrypted bucket if needed.

Date: Fri, 08 May 2027 10:21:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + action items: multilingual model-fit and eval plan

Karthik / Neha — thanks, that all sounds sensible. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset transfer — we will provision an S3 bucket and share credentials (will be available Monday). Expect ~600 DE, 600 SV, 400 FI labeled examples to start. We can add more once the rubric is signed off.
2) For the initial run we’d prefer Redwood to run the sampling eval and provide the confusion matrices and scripts so we can replicate locally.
3) Timeline ask: can you deliver the rubric and first-pass report within 5 business days of data receipt? Our legal is pushing for a short pilot window, so speed helps.
4) One more ask: can you do a small targeted test (500 examples) focusing only on German + Swedish to triage the compound-splitting issue you flagged before we hand over FI?

On Wed, 06 May 2027, Neha Kapoor wrote:
> Karthik — thanks for the thorough summary. Looping Marissa to own the eval rubric and initial run. Quick internal split of responsibilities so we’re aligned before Oliver confirms dataset transfer: 

Sounds good — we’ll proceed as requested.

Best,
Oliver

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + action items: multilingual model-fit and eval plan

Oliver — perfect, thanks for the quick confirmation and the preliminary counts. To confirm and close the loop: 

- We will accept S3 transfer — please send credentials to secure@redwood.ai and share the bucket path.
- Marissa will run the 500 German+Swedish triage as a priority as soon as data lands; target: initial tranche results in 3 business days from upload.
- Deliverable commitment: rubric + sampling plan within 5 business days of data receipt; initial benchmark doc within 7 business days.
- We’ll spin up a small Dedicated canary (3x A100-equivalent) for the 72-hour run once the benchmark confirms model choice.

Attachments included for your reference: multilingual-benchmarks-brief.pdf (preview, 312KB) and fintech_promptset_v1.csv (seed prompts).

If that matches your expectation I’ll have Neha share the SOW draft and Marissa will post the rubric link when ready.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.
Karthik
